title: Corner radius scale and consistency
when: The user wants rounded corners consistent across buttons, inputs, cards and images, or has picked a soft or sharp look.
inputs: the shape personality: sharp, soft or round
prompt:
Goal: A three or four step radius scale tied to element size, with nested corners that stay concentric.
Steps:
1. Choose the brand shape for medium elements: sharp 2 px, soft 6 to 8 px, round 12 to 16 px.
2. Define --radius-sm (inputs, tags), --radius-md (buttons, cards), --radius-lg (dialogs, sheets) and --radius-pill: 999px for chips.
3. Scale radius with size: a large card with 4 px looks sharp; a small chip with 16 px becomes a pill.
4. Nest correctly: inner radius equals outer radius minus the padding between them (16 px card with 8 px padding holds an 8 px image).
5. Clip images in rounded cards with overflow: hidden on the card, or give the img the inner radius.
6. Inputs and buttons that share a row use the same radius.
Quality bar:
- Every border-radius uses a token.
- Nested corners look parallel.
- Focus outlines follow the shape with outline-offset.
Pitfalls:
- Five different radii on one screen.
- Square image corners poking out of a rounded card.
- Pill shapes on large text blocks.
Verify:
- [ ] Radius tokens on :root.
- [ ] No raw radius values except 0.
- [ ] Inner radii computed from outer minus padding.
- [ ] Input and button radii match.
Output: Radius tokens and rules in style.css.

examples.input: I want a soft rounded look across the app
examples.output: --radius-sm 4px, --radius-md 8px, --radius-lg 16px, pill chips, card images at 8px inside 8px padding
